claims.text: All three transactional artifacts describe the same trip, which discharges the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) before any threshold is reached: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown each carry trip_id TRP-09112, and the gps_trace's first fix (2026-09-19T14:10:00+08:00) matches the trip_record's started_at to the second, so the trace the rider measures against is the trace of this trip and not of some other job.

On the measurement POL-RD-01 makes governing, the trip is longer than the route shown at booking. POL-RD-01 fixes gps_trace.trace_distance_km as the governing field and forbids citing the trip_record's rounded copy of the same measurement for the threshold test; the trace reads 11.5 km against a booking-time optimal of 10.0 km, an excess of 1.5 km. The absolute limb of the POL-RD-01 test (greater than 0.8 km) is satisfied at almost twice the required margin.

The 1.5 km is not a sampling artefact and nothing justifies discounting it. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 133 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum interval gap of 0.0 seconds, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 are not engaged at all and the measurement stands at the artifact's full admissibility weight of 1.0 rather than being down-weighted under POL-GEN-02.

The additional distance was not asked for by the rider, so the driver cannot lay it at the rider's door. The chat log for this trip holds exactly one message, sent by the rider at 14:21:40, reading 'This looks a little longer than the route shown at booking.'; its waypoint_hint is null and no road or place is named. Under POL-RD-04 no rider instruction is recorded, no waypoint can be tested, and no part of the excess is excluded as rider-requested.

No external event explains the excess either, and the rider discloses the state of the one artifact that could have. EV-ADVIS-09112-01, the traffic advisory slot for this route and window, is MISSING: it carries issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, severity BLOCKING, weight 0.0 and no payload. Its absence is itself citable, and it establishes that no advisory covers the booked route and trip window, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and no closure, contraflow or junction works excuse any part of the 1.5 km. The rider relies on this artifact only for its absence and not for any positive fact.

The baseline the rider measures against is the correct one and nothing in the record shifts it. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so POL-RD-05 has no amendment to re-quote against; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and the booking-time optimal of 10.0 km stands as the only baseline in play.

The rider's profile gives the tribunal no ground to demand corroboration beyond the trace: deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 rider-side trigger (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is not met and the extra-corroboration requirement is not engaged. The rider's remaining counters — prior_no_show_flags 1, prior_disputes_filed 1, prior_disputes_upheld 0 — are context only under POL-GEN-01 and may not carry any finding against the rider.

The driver's counter-statement that he 'stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop' names no artifact and no clause, and the in-trip chat log records no driver message at all. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded, so nothing in the bundle contradicts the 1.5 km excess measured on the trace.

If the excess is treated as established, the remedy is arithmetic and the rider's claimed SGD 1.69 is exactly it: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 10.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 20.0 optimal min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0, read from the fare_breakdown, which is the only artifact carrying that field) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP on the optimal route + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo discount = 17.70. Refund = 19.39 charged_total - 17.70 = 1.69, rounded up to SGD 1.70. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and only 8.72% of charged_total, so the outcome would be PARTIAL_REFUND and not a full refund; and with erp_gantries empty and off-route ERP totalling 0.00 there is no pass-through line to add on top under POL-RD-09.

The rider does not contend that the measured excess clears POL-RD-01 as written: 1.5 km is 15.0% of the 10.0 km optimal, short of the 20% limb, and both limbs must pass. The rider's submission is that the excess is nonetheless real, measured on an unimpaired trace, and unexplained by anything in the bundle — no rider instruction, no amendment, no closure, and the sole explanatory artifact EV-ADVIS-09112-01 missing (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0). On that record the rider asks that, if the tribunal does not apply the POL-RD-02 arithmetic above, the contested SGD 1.69 be held for a human reviewer under POL-RD-10 rather than left standing as collected, because the gap in the record is a data failure and not a finding that the extra distance was properly chargeable.

claims.text: The measured excess on this trip is 1.5 km against a 10.0 km optimal route — 15.00% of optimal, as derived in code from the trace itself (derived.deviation.excess_pct). POL-RD-01 establishes a route deviation only where the excess is greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km; 15.00% is below the 20% gate, so no deviation is established and the clause directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01's two limbs are conjunctive, not alternative. The absolute limb is met — 1.5 km is above the 0.8 km threshold_km — but the clause requires BOTH tests to pass, and states expressly that if either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION. The rider's '1.5 km longer' is therefore not a deviation in policy terms; it is an excess that fails the percentage limb by 5 points.

There is no distance-field disagreement for the rider to exploit: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 11.5 km, which is the governing field under POL-RD-01, and the trip_record's actual_distance_km is the same 11.5 km — a rounded convenience copy. Use the governing figure and the excess is still 1.5 km / 15.00%.

The trace cannot be attacked as impaired or incomplete: it carries 133 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds, and its admissibility is COMPLETE at weight 1.0. The rider therefore cannot route around the threshold via POL-RD-07, and the no-corroboration escalation trigger in POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The initial burden under POL-RD-08 sits with the rider: she must show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. On the unimpaired trace the excess is 15.00%, short of the 20% gate, so the burden is never discharged and the driver is never called on to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12.

The optimal distance is the platform's stored booking estimate — the routing-engine-v3.2 snapshot at 10.0 km — which is the figure POL-RD-01 directs be used. No relocation re-quote applies: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 does not disturb the baseline and the 20% gate remains 2.0 km, which the 1.5 km excess cannot reach.

The one refund route that survives a failed POL-RD-01 test — a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) — is closed on this record. The fare breakdown charges no ERP gantries (erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp 0.0) and applies no airport surcharge (0.0 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport), so there is no phantom line to refund in full regardless of deviation.

No repeat-pattern uplift or conduct referral is available against the driver. POL-RD-06 is engaged only by a MATERIAL deviation, and a 15.00% excess of 1.5 km is neither greater than 50% of optimal nor greater than 8.0 km. In any event the driver profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610 — nowhere near the 3-flag or 0.05-ratio pattern test — so the citable profile fields add nothing against him.

The chat log does not carry the rider's case either. The sole message is her own mid-trip remark that the trip 'looks a little longer'; it names no place and no road and carries a null waypoint_hint, so under POL-RD-04 it neither records a rider-requested detour nor corroborates any excess, and the requirement to use the waypoint_hint field rather than geocode a place name means the corroboration test cannot be run at all. The driver's account — ordinary through roads, no additional stop — stands unrebutted.

ruling.explanation: Rider: your complaint is that the trip was 1.5 km longer than the 10.0 km route shown at booking. That measurement is solid — the GPS trace is complete (133 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps) and both the trace and the trip record read the same 11.5 km. But POL-RD-01 treats a route as deviated only when the excess is BOTH more than 0.8 km AND more than 20% of the optimal distance. Your 1.5 km clears the distance limb but is only 15% of 10.0 km, so the percentage limb fails. The two limbs are conjunctive, and the policy says expressly that if either fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. So the fare stands as charged. No other route to a refund opens: your single chat message (14:21:40) names no place or road and its waypoint_hint is null, so no rider-requested detour can be found (POL-RD-04); there was no pickup or dropoff amendment (pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null, POL-RD-05); the trip was RYDE_X, not a pooled itinerary (POL-RD-12); and the one refund that does not need a deviation — a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) — is closed, because the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries and no airport surcharge. Driver: your account that you stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop is consistent with the record, and no conduct referral applies — your deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 610 completed trips in 90 days, far from the POL-RD-06 pattern test, which is in any event only engaged by a material deviation that this trip does not have. On escalation: I have not sent this to a human reviewer. None of POL-RD-10's triggers fires. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07 (no gap over 90s, no jump over 500 m, sampling interval 10s), the trip identifiers and timestamps agree across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, no exculpatory clause is asserted against a missing artifact, and the fare has no unmatched charge line. EV-ADVIS-09112-01, the traffic advisory slot, is MISSING at weight 0.0 — it can carry no fact and is citable only for its absence, which merely confirms no closure defence could be run; that does not disturb the threshold result. The rider's request that the contested amount be held for a reviewer is declined: a failed threshold is a finding, not a data gap. The profile fields either side mentioned that are not the citable counters (rating, account age, lifetime trips, prior disputes, prior flags) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and carried no weight in this decision.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the fare stands as charged; no refund and no compensation is due.

The measurement itself is not in dispute. The GPS trace of this trip (EV-GPS-09112) records 11.5 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff, at a clean 133 fixes over a 10-second interval with no gaps and full coverage. The optimal route stored at booking (EV-TRIP-09112) is 10.0 km. The excess is therefore 1.5 km, or 15.0% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 makes the deviation test conjunctive: the excess must exceed 20% of optimal_distance_km AND exceed 0.8 km, and if either limb fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. The absolute limb is cleared at 1.5 km, but 15.0% falls short of the 20% gate. That is the finding.

To the rider: your submission that the extra 1.5 km is real, measured on an unimpaired trace, is accepted. But because the POL-RD-01 threshold is not met, the POL-RD-02 recomputation you offer (charged_total 19.39 less recomputed_fare 17.70, a 1.69 refund rounded up to 1.70) never becomes payable and no distance-or-time refund runs. The one refund route that survives a failed threshold — a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) — is closed on this record: the fare breakdown charges no ERP gantries (erp_gantries empty) and no airport surcharge, so there is no phantom line to refund. Your alternative request that the contested SGD 1.69 be held for a human reviewer under POL-RD-10 also cannot be granted, because none of POL-RD-10's triggers fires. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) (no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m, sampling interval 10 s), so the no-corroboration escalation of POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; the trip identifiers and pickup timestamps across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all match; no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing artifact — POL-RD-03 was not asserted by the driver, so your citation of the missing advisory does not fit POL-RD-10(5); the refund is nowhere near the ceiling; and every fare line has a counterpart in the trace or trip record. The absence of a traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09112-01, MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0 — disclosed) is citable as you say, but it operates in your favour by closing off any closure excuse; it does not open an escalation.

To the driver: your account is accepted. The trace is unimpaired, no deviation is established, and nothing adverse is found against you. The chat log holds no rider instruction (POL-RD-04), there is no pickup or dropoff amendment (POL-RD-05) and the vehicle type is not pooled (POL-RD-12), so the 10.0 km baseline stands undisturbed. Your profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern — deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 610 — and the excess is not MATERIAL, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no conduct referral arises.

No referral is issued, because no clause on this record produces one. The rider's remaining profile counters (prior_no_show_flags, prior_disputes_filed, prior_disputes_upheld) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and carry no finding in either direction.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the fare you were charged stands. Here is why.

What the record shows. The trip (TRP-09112) ran 11.5 km on the governing measurement — gps_trace.trace_distance_km on EV-GPS-09112, which POL-RD-01 makes the field that decides, with the trip_record's identical 11.5 km being only a rounded copy. The booking-time optimal on EV-TRIP-09112 is 10.0 km. The excess is therefore 1.5 km, which is 15.0% of the optimal route.

To the rider. Your reading of the distance is correct: the trip really was about 1.5 km longer than the route shown at booking. But POL-RD-01 does not make every longer trip refundable. It requires BOTH limbs to pass — an excess greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km. Your 1.5 km clears the absolute limb but is 15.0%, five points short of the percentage limb, and the clause says expressly that if either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. The claim for SGD 1.69 is therefore not payable.

Your fallback arguments do not change that. The POL-RD-02 recomputation you set out is correct arithmetic — recomputed_fare 17.70 against a charged_total of 19.39 — but that clause only runs once a deviation is established, and it was not; there is nothing to recompute against. Your request that the SGD 1.69 be held for a human reviewer under POL-RD-10 is refused because none of that clause's triggers fires: the trace is unimpaired, the trip identifiers and timestamps agree across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing artifact, the computed refund does not exceed SGD 150 or the charged total, and no fare line is unmatched. A gap you would like filled is not the same as a mandatory escalation, and NO_ACTION here means the charge stands, not that anything is added to it.

To the driver. Your position is upheld. The excess does not reach the POL-RD-01 gate, so the question of exoneration never arises and no adverse finding attaches to this trip. POL-RD-06 is not engaged — a 15.0% / 1.5 km excess is neither a material deviation (over 50% or over 8.0 km) nor is there any repeat pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 610 completed trips in 90 days) — so no conduct referral is made. Your statement that you stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop is consistent with the record and is not rebutted by anything in the bundle.

On the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09112-01, MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0): it carries no fact and decides nothing here, because no closure was asserted in your defence and, no deviation having been established, POL-RD-03 has no work to do. The trace itself is sound — 133 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps — and is not impaired under POL-RD-07 or down-weighted under POL-GEN-02. The finding rests on artifacts at full weight, so confidence in this ruling is high.

ruling.explanation:
The governing measurement is not in dispute, and it decides this case on POL-RD-01's threshold. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that governs, and the trace reads 11.5 km against the booking-time optimal of 10.0 km — an excess of 1.5 km, or 15.0% of optimal (both advocates adopt these figures, and the derived deviation carries them). POL-RD-01 establishes a route deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of optimal (2.0 km here) AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The absolute limb passes at 1.5 km; the percentage limb fails at 15.0% against a 20% gate, and the clause is explicit that the two limbs are conjunctive and that if either establishment test fails there is no deviation and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. So the outcome is NO_ACTION and the present state of the charge stands.

To the rider: I have not discounted your measurement. The trace is unimpaired — 133 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps, maximum inter-fix gap 0.0 s — so it does not engage POL-RD-07(a)–(c) and it is admitted at its full admissibility weight of 1.0; there is nothing to down-weight and no POL-RD-10(3) data failure. Your 1.5 km is real, and it is simply below the gate the policy sets. Your alternative request — run the POL-RD-02 arithmetic — cannot run: POL-RD-02 applies only where a deviation is first established under POL-RD-01, and none is. The figure you arrive at (charged_total 19.39 less a recomputed fare of 17.70 = 1.69, rounded up to 1.70) is the correct arithmetic for a deviation that the threshold test has not found. Your further request that the SGD 1.69 be held for a human reviewer under POL-RD-10 is declined because no POL-RD-10 trigger fires: identifiers and timestamps match across the artifacts, the trace is unimpaired, no exculpatory clause is asserted against an absent artifact, no fare line lacks a counterpart, and no two admissible artifacts are in mutually contradictory balance. The one gap in the record is the traffic-advisory slot EV-ADVIS-09112-01 (status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0). Its absence is citable and is cited: it means no POL-RD-03 closure exoneration is available. But an advisory could not have moved the 11.5 km trace or the 10.0 km optimal — the 15% figure would be the same with a full advisory in the pool — so its absence creates no uncertainty about the test this case turns on. That is a question for the record's completeness, not a reason to hold the charge.

To the driver: the rider's evidence fails the threshold on its own terms, so nothing further is needed from you. Your counter-statement that you 'stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop' carries no evidence ID and therefore no weight under POL-RD-08; it is not relied on, and it does not need to be, because the outcome rests on the rider's own unimpaired trace. No exculpatory clause is engaged: there is no amendment re-quote (POL-RD-05: pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null), the vehicle is RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply, and POL-RD-04's rider-detour test cannot be run (the single chat message is the rider's own mid-trip remark, naming no place or road, with a null waypoint_hint).

No clause produces a referral, and none produces a payment. POL-RD-06 is not engaged: a 15.0%/1.5 km excess is not a MATERIAL deviation (neither greater than 50% of optimal nor greater than 8.0 km), and the driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against 610 completed trips, so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged: the fare breakdown charges no ERP gantries and applies no airport surcharge, so there is no phantom line to refund as a billing-integrity correction. No driver compensation arises either: the billed distance (11.5 km) equals the trace distance, so there is no unbilled shortfall under POL-RD-04. The driver's profile fields cited (deviation_flags_90d, completed_trips_90d) were used only for the POL-RD-06 test, and the rider's context-only counters (prior_no_show_flags, prior_disputes_filed, prior_disputes_upheld) carried no finding against her.
